body.estimand_functional: \((p,G)\longmapsto\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\setminus\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\), with \(\mathsf{Cov}_p\) evaluated chamberwise through \(\mathcal E_p\) and \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}\) evaluated by the terminal actual-row certificates.

sampling_model.design: Population identification from one baseline and one unknown-target single-node soft-intervention context per latent node under noninjective mixing \(2\le p<q\).
sampling_model.units: Inputs are aligned population factorization data \(\mathcal R\) and the \(q+1\) population covariance matrices \(\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\); there is no finite-sample claim.
sampling_model.treatment: Each non-source context changes every incoming coefficient of one unknown latent target and retains every such edge. Targets are identified only up to one common latent permutation.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition applies. Baseline and intervention variances are positive and may coincide. Covariance theorems use only declared finite generic loci, including \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\ne0\), cover both adjacent sign chambers, and make no pointwise claim on neutral hyperplanes.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Aligned factor directions and source laws modulo common permutation and diagonal scaling are population inputs. Recovery from raw laws and finite-sample tensor estimation are outside scope.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Equation (20) derives compatibility ranks from the actual \(\Delta^{(k)}_{k,\cdot}\) rows, Definition 3.14 uses baseline inverse-path ranks, and Theorem 3.15 claims the two rank tests are generically equivalent.
Problem 5.2 asks whether the higher-cumulant-compatible graph class is strictly contained in the covariance-compatible graph class.
The generic-soft covariance analysis and perfect-intervention graph-recovery clause are stated for injective mixing \(p\ge q\).
The paper treats unpaired observational and interventional data under generalized faithfulness and recovers an equivalence class.
Theorem 2.8 characterizes generic covariance-submatrix rank by trek separation.
The half-trek criterion supplies a polynomial-time sufficient certificate for generic rational identifiability.
The paper studies half-trek criteria for identifiability of latent-variable models.
Sections IV--V provide semidefinite tests and positive-semidefinite decomposition and realization machinery for latent causal structures.

In arXiv:2410.23102v1, Theorem 3.10 transfers a semialgebraic image through an affine-birational parametrization with positive localizing denominators, and Theorem 3.11 identifies its saturated vanishing ideal.

The paper uses tree dynamic programming over the primal graph of variables co-occurring in atomic constraints to accelerate existential Fourier--Motzkin elimination and cylindrical algebraic decomposition.

body.tldr: Actual soft-intervention rows \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\) admit the proved terminal-copy and affine-support compatibility test. In the noninjective regime \(2\le p<q\), regular covariance twins are exactly a finite union of positive-real factor-line projections. For the \(p=2,q=4\) fork, all eight branches reduce losslessly to two candidate scalars and reconstruct the original five covariance equations; the positive rational \(T\)-family is valid but supplies only local realizations. The required all-chamber projection classification is not proved, so the bounded-width realization-or-separator compiler and its complexity headline are retracted. The prospective LCD workflow can report the corrected actual-row class and enumerate covariance alternatives, but it cannot yet certify whether higher cumulants remove all covariance alternatives.

project_justification.gap: Problem 5.2 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal asks whether covariance and higher-cumulant information distinguish compatible graph classes. After correcting Definition 3.14 to use actual intervention rows, the noninjective covariance question becomes density of a union of positive-real projected branches in every full-dimensional sign-and-variance chamber. Existing linkage, positive-semidefinite realization, half-trek, and generic real-elimination results do not supply the required graph-specific non-quantifier-elimination density certificate.
project_justification.niche: The proved contribution isolates the exact obstruction. Terminal compatibility has finite linkage and affine certificates, while every regular covariance twin belongs to one of at most \(2^{q-r}\) factor-line systems. The four-node fork is reduced exactly to eight bivariate systems, including all positivity, denominator, support, retention, mixing, and covariance equations. What remains is global projection geometry over all true parameters, not another local witness.
project_justification.fill: The paper delivers the corrected terminal algorithm, the exact covariance-branch reduction, the complete regular two-scalar fork reduction, and a positive rational covariance collision verified in all five contexts. It also proves that the rational family and local regularity cannot decide chamberwise density. Because the fork projection gate remains unresolved, no bounded-width compiler, certificate-height bound, pathwidth guarantee, all-graph criterion, or generic strictness family is claimed.

body.related_work: Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025) derive the actual intervention-row system in Equation (20), use the observational inverse-path class in Definition 3.14, state recovery through Theorem 1.7, and pose graph and covariance questions in Problems 5.1--5.2. The terminal-copy result repairs the mismatch between the actual rows and the observational-path substitution. Squires, Seigal, Bhate, and Uhler (2023) recover transitive-closure information for injective soft-intervention models; their injective result does not decide the noninjective positive-real covariance projection considered here. Half-trek, semidefinite realization, affine-birational transfer, and tree-accelerated quantifier-elimination work remain methodological context. In particular, no complexity comparison is claimed for the retracted covariance-terminal-width compiler, because no theorem translates its proposed frontier state into a projection-complete elimination invariant.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Exact symbolic verification confirms all five covariance equalities for the rational fork family, positivity of the candidate variances \(T+144/121\) and \(19/4\), the actual-row obstruction, and rank-three regularity of all eight loading choices at audited points. The proof also reconstructs every legal solution of the eight systems back into the original covariance equations. These facts do not classify the union's projection over a full true chamber. The proposed bounded-width definitions do not specify a gluing invariant, prevent elimination fill-in beyond a bag, or derive the advertised bit and coefficient bounds; using unrestricted real quantifier elimination would violate the requested structural criterion.
body.honest_scope: All covariance-frontier claims remain in the noninjective regime \(2\le p<q\), on the declared theorem-specific generic loci and full-dimensional sign-and-variance chambers. Candidate twins may be variance-neutral, both signs of each true variance change are retained, and no pointwise claim is made on excluded true neutral hyperplanes. The terminal actual-row theorem is exact and independent of variance activity. The fork theorem is a sound-and-complete regular reduction to eight bivariate systems, not an all-chamber feasibility classification. The rational \(T\)-family proves a positive covariance collision and local robustness only. The bounded-width compiler, realization-or-separator output, bit complexity, coefficient growth, pathwidth implication, all-graph positive-real criterion, and infinite generic-strictness families are not established. The prospective workflow may output corrected terminal compatibility and verified individual covariance twins, but not a global high-cumulant information-frontier verdict.
body.interpretation: The corrected compatible graph set is operational at population level once the aligned factor rows are available. Covariance-only alternatives are also represented exactly by finite branch systems, so any displayed candidate can be checked against every context covariance. However, the existence of the worked fork collision does not establish generic covariance surplus, and failure of selected branches does not establish equality. Until the full chamberwise projected union is certified, the LCD consumer must report this distinction as unresolved rather than asserting that higher cumulants genuinely remove covariance alternatives.
